questions.question: Define a micro-organism. A bacterium is 2 micrometres long and a virus is 100 nanometres across. How many of the viruses would fit along the bacterium, and which microscope is needed to see each?
questions.expected_answer: A micro-organism is a living thing too small to be seen clearly without a microscope. 2 micrometres = 2 000 nanometres, and 2 000 ÷ 100 = 20, so 20 viruses fit along the bacterium. The bacterium can be seen with a light microscope at high magnification; the virus is too small for a light microscope and needs an electron microscope.

questions.question: Compare viruses and bacteria under the headings structure, reproduction and examples, and explain why antibiotics cure bacterial infections but not viral ones.
questions.expected_answer: Structure: a virus is not a cell, only genetic material (DNA or RNA) in a protein coat; a bacterium is a single cell with a cell wall, membrane and cytoplasm but no nucleus, its DNA free in the cytoplasm. Reproduction: a virus reproduces only inside a living host cell, taking over the cell to make copies; a bacterium reproduces by binary fission, splitting into two, as often as every 20 minutes. Examples: viruses — HIV, influenza, measles, rabies, the COVID-19 coronavirus; bacteria — TB bacterium, cholera bacterium, yoghurt bacteria. Antibiotics attack structures such as the bacterial cell wall that viruses lack, and viruses hide inside the body's own cells, so antibiotics have no effect on them.

questions.question: Describe protists and fungi, naming three protists and two fungi with one feature of each. A single bacterium divides every 20 minutes: how many bacteria are there after 3 hours?
questions.expected_answer: Protists: mostly single cells with a nucleus. Amoeba moves and feeds with pseudopodia; paramecium moves with cilia; euglena has a flagellum and chloroplasts so it can photosynthesise; Plasmodium is a parasite that causes malaria. Fungi: cells with a nucleus and chitin cell walls, no chlorophyll, feed by releasing enzymes and absorbing digested food. Yeast is single-celled and reproduces by budding; moulds such as Rhizopus and Penicillium are made of hyphae forming a mycelium and reproduce by spores. 3 hours = 9 divisions, so 2 to the power 9 = 512 bacteria.
